# RFC 9921 fixtures

The two RFC 3161 timestamp tokens of [RFC 9921](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9921.html) Appendix A, as the
DER the `3161-ttc` and `3161-ctt` header parameters carry.

[cose-wg/Examples](https://github.com/cose-wg/Examples), vendored under [`../cose-wg/`](../cose-wg/), has no vector
for RFC 9921 (checked at upstream commit `53c9d634`, still its head on 2026-09-13). The RFC publishes its examples in
CBOR diagnostic notation only; the two byte strings below are the `h'...'` literals of the appendix, re-joined across
the line wrapping of the text rendering and otherwise untouched.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | [RFC 9921](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9921.txt), Appendix A.1 (label 269) and A.2 (label 270), February 2026 |
| Extractor | [`extract.py`](extract.py), in this directory |
| Cross-check | byte-identical to `example/ttc/ttc-tst.der` and `example/ctt/ctt-tst.der` of the draft's source repository, [ietf-scitt/draft-birkholz-cose-tsa-tst-header-parameter](https://github.com/ietf-scitt/draft-birkholz-cose-tsa-tst-header-parameter) |
| Produced on | 2026-09-13 |

Both tokens were issued by the public TSA of [freetsa.org](https://freetsa.org) on 2025-08-29 under its policy
`1.2.3.4.1`, with SHA-256 imprints and `certReq` set, and carry the TSA's certificate chain; hence the 5453 bytes
each. Nothing is verified about that chain here: the library reads the `TSTInfo` and binds the imprint, and leaves
the CMS validation to the application.

| File | Header parameter | `MessageImprint.hashedMessage` | Is the SHA-256 of |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ttc-tst.der` | `3161-ttc` (269, protected) | `09e638d4 ... aae3f6b0` | the payload bytes `'This is the content.'`, as RFC 9921 §3.2 requires |
| `ctt-tst.der` | `3161-ctt` (270, unprotected) | `dd9471ef ... 3eeaf7c8` | see below |

## The `3161-ctt` token of Appendix A.2 does not match its own message

RFC 9921 §3.1.1 computes the CTT imprint of the COSE_Sign1 of RFC 9052 Appendix C.2.1 (the same message Appendix
A.2 starts from): SHA-256 over the CBOR-encoded `signature` field, `0x5840` followed by the 64 signature bytes, is
`44c2419d ... 54763b4e`. The TimeStampReq and the token of Appendix A.2, however, carry `dd9471ef ... 3eeaf7c8`.

The cause is in the generator of the example, `example/ctt/create-example.sh` of the source repository. It reads
the signature out of `in.diag` with `awk '/signature/ {print $4}'` and pipes it through `diag2cbor.rb` to obtain
the bytes to hash. Commit `58407a7b` (2025-05-12, "apply line folding on synthesis") folded `in.diag` at 69 columns,
so the signature literal spans three lines and `awk` now yields only the first, `h'8eb33e4c ... 083106c4d`, an
unterminated literal. `diag2cbor.rb` (cbor-diag 0.11.8) rejects it and prints an error; the script's `set -o
pipefail` does not reach into the process substitution, so the error text is what `openssl ts -query -data` hashed
when commit `086f7f79` (2025-08-29, "update CTT examples") regenerated the token. The 200-byte error message is
reproduced verbatim in `tests/Structure/Timestamp/Rfc9921ExamplesTest.php`; its SHA-256 is `dd9471ef ...
3eeaf7c8`. The token of Appendix A.1, generated by a script that hashes a literal string, is unaffected.

The test suite therefore checks the `3161-ctt` mode against §3.1.1 and §3.1.2, whose imprints are the ones the
normative text of §3.1 produces, and uses `ctt-tst.der` for what it is: a well-formed token that decodes, and that
the binding check correctly refuses for the message it is attached to. An erratum against Appendix A.2, with the
account above as its notes, was reported to the RFC Editor on 2026-09-13; it is listed at
<https://www.rfc-editor.org/errata/rfc9921> once the RFC Production Center has screened it.
